definition: OpenHands, formerly known as OpenDevin, is an open-source artificial intelligence agent and platform for AI-assisted software development.
details: It uses large language models to perform software-engineering tasks such as modifying source code, executing commands, browsing the web and interacting with development tools. OpenHands is model-agnostic and can be configured to use different cloud-hosted or locally hosted language models.

explainer.lead: OpenHands, formerly OpenDevin, is an open-source AI agent and platform for AI-assisted software development. It matters because it is model-agnostic, so the same agent can be pointed at different cloud-hosted or locally hosted models.

tiers.eli5: It is a free coding helper that can edit code, run commands and look things up online, and you can choose which AI brain it uses.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers configure it with a cloud-hosted or locally hosted LLM and let it modify source code, execute commands, browse the web and interact with development tools. The pitfall is that its behavior depends on the model you plug in.
tiers.paperLevel: An open-source agent and platform for AI-assisted software development that uses large language models to perform software-engineering tasks. It is model-agnostic, supporting cloud-hosted and local models.

explainer.example: A team can pair OpenHands with a locally hosted model to keep code on their own machines while it edits files and runs commands.
